en: Furthermore, having sprinkled the mandala site with water from all the jars while reciting the mantra *oṃ sarvasaṃśodhani hūṃ phaṭ*, having purified it and smeared it with fragrance, and having scattered flowers outside, one should—relying upon the mandala to be drawn situated in the expanse of the sky—worship it preceded by the offering of *argha* (and praise). Then, the practitioner himself, possessing the yoga, should visualize the assistant as the form of Vairocana or another [Buddha], and [visualize] the syllable *jaḥ* arising in the right and left eyes of both himself and that [assistant].

Having visualized the moon and sun as having a yellow radiance, holding that thread with the left vajra-fist at the navel while standing in the even posture (*samapada*), [the master] sends forth that assistant practitioner who likewise holds the thread with the three syllables *jjaḥ jjaḥ jjaḥ*. Then, having been drawn back by the assistant practitioner with the three syllables *jjaḥ jjaḥ jjaḥ*, and while both stand facing each other in that same manner—the one situated in the west facing east and the one situated in the south facing north—the two Brahma-threads are placed at the level of the navel in the intermediate space.
Causing [the thread] to fall, one should take up the thread with the thumb and finger of the right hand holding a vajra and make the snapping sound (*ācchaṭā*).

Again, having sprinkled [the area] with water from all the vases while reciting the mantra *oṃ sarvasaṃśodhani hūṃ phaṭ*, and having smeared it with fragrant substances so that it is pure, one should scatter flowers upon the site.

Visualizing the maṇḍala that abides in the center of space as being clearly present, one performs worship preceded by the offering of arghya, and having offered praise, one—endowed with the yoga of that [deity]—meditates on the companions for accomplishment in the forms of Vairocana and the others.

Visualize one's own right and left eyes as the sun and moon, born from the syllable *dzraḥ*, possessing yellow rays of light. Standing in the even-legged posture (*samapada*), hold the marking cord with the vajra-fist of the left hand at the navel; likewise, the ritual assistant who holds the cord should [recite] *dzraḥ dzraḥ dzraḥ*.

Urged by the three syllables, the practice assistant also leads with the three syllables *dzdzaḥ dzdzaḥ dzdzaḥ*, and remaining in that same manner facing [the center], one situated in the west facing east and one situated in the south facing north extend the two Brahma-lines across the navel level in the space before them.
Holding the marking cord with the thumb and fingers of the right hand, which is joined with a vajra, one should strike it while making the sound of snapping the fingers.
And for all the laying down of the lines, one should recite: *oṃ vajrasamaya sūtraṃ mātikrama hūṃ hūṃ oṃ svā āḥ hā*.
For all the marking of the boundary-lines as well, one should recite: *oṃ vajrasamaya sūtraṃ mātikrama hūṃ hūṃ oṃ svā āḥ hā*.

"For this sound, it is now the time for you to come here for the sake of sentient beings"—this is the conventional meaning [of the passage]: that all Tathāgatas, drawn by the sound of the *sūtra*, having assembled, become included within the *sūtras*.

"This sound is the time for you to act for the sake of sentient beings; therefore, come here! and so forth. This is the symbolic meaning: one should meditate that all the Tathāgatas, invited by the sound of the *śūla* (line), arrive together and dissolve into the lines.

In all cases, the preceptor and the assistant practitioner should proceed clockwise; however, in the mandala of Śrī Saṃvara and in the mandala of Śrī Vajravārāhī, they should proceed counter-clockwise and face toward all directions with equanimity.

In all cases, one should proceed by circling clockwise around the preceptor and the companions in the practice; however, for the mandala of Śrī Saṃvara and the mandala of Śrī Vajravārāhī, one should proceed by circling counter-clockwise. One should cultivate the conviction that all directions are equal.
This is the procedure for laying out the lines in space.
Thus concludes the ritual for marking the lines in space.
